title: Self‑Serve Network Preflight + Temporary Proxy Bridge for Air‑gapped/VPC Intake
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Enterprise customers requesting Private/VPC/on‑prem deployments frequently block on networking and upgrade constraints (firewall rules, proxying, outbound allowlists, and temporary patch windows). Current intake is manual and high‑touch: Solutions Engineers run ad hoc checks and coordinate engineers for short‑lived exceptions, which scales poorly and increases time‑to‑decision. This ticket scopes a productized intake path: 1) a customer-facing self‑serve preflight diagnostic that runs non-invasive checks and generates a compatibility report, 2) an internal temporary ‘proxy bridge’ SOP for controlled short‑term exceptions (for customers that cannot open outbound but can accept a controlled reverse‑tunnel/temporary proxy), and 3) a prioritization rubric that routes requests to fast‑lane, standard, or remediation lanes based on risk, compliance, and business impact.
acceptance_criteria: Customer preflight UI with downloadable compatibility report (JSON + human summary) covering network ports, DNS resolution, cert validation, and minimal OS/package checks

Preflight output maps to intake buckets: Fastlane (low risk, auto-approve), Standard (requires SE review), Remediation (requires engineering/network remediation), plus an explicit 'Proxy Bridge candidate' flag
Internal proxy bridge playbook documented with security checklists, timeboxed approvals, and automatic revoke hooks (playbook link included)
Routing rules implemented in intake dashboard to assign SLA (24h, 5d, 15d) and surface risk notes to Solutions/SEs
Telemetry: preflight run count, pass/fail rates, time-to-triage per bucket, and customer satisfaction survey attached to the report
notes: Tradeoffs considered: building a full agent vs. lightweight remote checks. We chose lightweight checks (DNS, port TCP handshake, TLS chain validation) to avoid install/agent friction for initial rollout.

Proxy bridge is explicitly temporary and requires CISO approval for customers with high regulatory requirements. Bridge is implemented as customer-provided reverse SSH tunnel or vendor-managed reverse proxy depending on their security posture.
We must coordinate with Security + Legal on data retention for preflight reports (they may include IPs, hostnames). Marked for security review as part of rollout.
Estimated engineering work: backend preflight service (2 sprint), front-end report UI (1 sprint), intake routing changes and dashboard (1 sprint), runbook & SE enablement (0.5 sprint).
